analysis:
The PR makes one code change, in NativeToolStreamRouter.swift (patch hunk at lines 182-188). In forced tool_choice mode (requiresToolCall), the router used to skip framing-only whitespace only when usesNativeChannels was true. It now skips it on every path, including legacy Qwen text without native channels. Other visible text still throws toolChoiceViolation. The docs say whitespace alone still counts as a missing call in ToolConstraintValidation.validate, and that other Unicode whitespace remains a violation (422).

The changed code only affects whether ASCII space, tab, CR and LF are dropped from provider output before a validated call. It does not touch encryption, attestation, authorization or the coordinator trust boundary. It does not expose prompts (A-001) or change any key custody. It adds no new input channel.

The skipped whitespace is not emitted, so this adds no plaintext leakage. It could slightly loosen enforcement because whitespace is dropped where it used to be a violation. That is a correctness and availability matter at most, and the provider is already an adversarial output source (T-007), so the consumer gets no cryptographic output guarantee either way.

The docs/architecture/inference.md changes (lines 2017-2040 head, plus the unchanged surrounding text in the supplied units) describe the tool_constraint_models advertisement per exact build via ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy.advertisesCapability. They are documentation only and do not change security controls. The remaining supplied doc text is unchanged context. I did not see the full isFramingWhitespace definition, and I did not see the advertisesCapability or structuredPostValidation implementations, so those are unverified. I could not confirm that the whitespace-only case still fails validation downstream, so I am only noting that gap and not reporting a finding. No finding is raised.
